The story

Brian has run marketing for local businesses for 26 years. And he also owns a bathroom remodeling company in New Orleans called TurnKey Bath Remodel.

He ran a small, controlled test in his own market: about $10,000 in data cost and labor, aimed at homeowners actually ready for a bathroom remodel.

It turned into $128,911 in signed bathroom contracts. Not a fluke platform month, a repeatable system he keeps running for his own shop today.

Now he runs that same system for a small number of other remodelers. He handles all of it, the ads and the calls. You don't learn it, you don't manage it. You take the booked jobs.

I'm not handing anybody a course. I run the same system for you that I run for my own bathroom company. You just answer when the job's ready.

Fair questions

What owners ask before they book

Do I have to learn or run anything?

No. Brian runs the entire system and his team handles the calls. There's no course, no dashboard, nothing to manage. Your only job is to answer when a booked homeowner is ready and show up to the estimate.

Is this a guarantee that I'll make $100K?

Depends. That $128,911 came from two things: the booked estimates and a team that closes at a high rate. Brian can put the estimates on your calendar. What they turn into depends on how well you close. On the call he'll look at your close rate and give you a straight read for your market.

Are these shared leads like Angi?

No. This is the opposite of the shared-lead auction. It's a done-for-you system Brian runs for a limited number of remodelers, so the jobs are yours, not sold to five contractors.

Does this only work in New Orleans?

New Orleans is a hard market to do this in. Median household income is about $56K, and more than 1 in 5 residents live below the poverty line. If homeowner data plus phone calls can sign $128,911 in bathroom work there, a wealthier metro isn't the problem. What Brian does check on the call is your specific market: the data available, your service area, and your job sizes.

Source: Data USA, New Orleans, LA

Who is Brian Hong?

Brian's been marketing local businesses since 2000. He founded Infintech Designs in New Orleans in 2002, a Google Premier Partner agency that's built 4,000+ websites, and he co-founded TurnKey Bath Remodel, a bathroom-remodeling company with 500+ bathrooms done. He built this system for his own bathroom company first, with his own money, before offering it to anyone else. So when he runs it for you, he's not testing a theory on your budget. He's running the thing he already depends on. And if it's not a fit for your business, he'll tell you that on the call.
